description: Reviewed semantic relationships between shell patterns. Decisions are based on user job and behavior, not visual similarity or a target component count.

jobs.job: Communicate a platform navigation, action, status, or inline control glyph on the canonical interface grid.
Represent one hosted application through artwork or a deterministic, theme-aware monogram.

decisions.rationale: Both render compact visual marks, but one labels shell controls while the other carries application identity and a deliberately larger colorful treatment.
decisions.substitutionBoundary: Never use AppIdentity as a generic action icon or PlatformIcon as hosted-app artwork.

jobs.job: Launch an application the current user already saved or built with minimum decision cost.
Evaluate an unfamiliar application before opening its detail surface.

decisions.rationale: Both present applications, but Home optimizes repeat launch while Explore carries discovery information and a different primary navigation contract.
decisions.substitutionBoundary: Share AppIdentity and status primitives, but do not add discovery metadata or detail-first behavior to HomeAppShortcut.

jobs.job: Name the screen the person is on and carry that screen's contextual actions.
Change global platform scope by choosing among the primary destinations, Node health and the utility footer.

decisions.rationale: Both are always-present shell chrome, but one answers "where am I and what can I do here" while the other answers "where else can I go". The bar hosts the drawer's trigger; it never duplicates its destinations.
decisions.substitutionBoundary: Do not place global destinations, Activity counts or Node status in the TopBar, and do not put screen names or per-screen actions in PlatformNavigation. The attention dot on the menu trigger is the only shared signal, and it never carries a number.

jobs.job: Identify the focused dApp and offer its reciprocal mode, overflow and Close controls.
Give one hosted dApp state a distinct, responsive card without repainting the surrounding platform shell.
Host the dApp and explain its lifecycle state — loading, offline with retry, unavailable or self-hosted — in the content area.

decisions.rationale: The bar owns route identity and actions, the hosted-app wrapper owns the responsive platform-to-app boundary, and the frame owns child-host lifecycle and permissions. The three compose without duplicating status, repainting navigation or moving application behavior into shell chrome.
decisions.substitutionBoundary: Do not present hosted-app status, retry affordances or iframe lifecycle messaging in the TopBar. Do not fetch, route or host the iframe in HostedAppStage. Do not put mode switching, Close, card geometry or platform navigation inside FocusedAppFrame.

jobs.job: Expose the complete platform information architecture, attention evidence, Node health and utility destinations through the Canvas drawer or desktop sidebar.
Switch among Home, Work and Search with persistent one-handed access on narrow screens.

decisions.rationale: Both change global platform scope, but the drawer is a complete map while the bottom Overlay is a deliberately fixed three-destination quick switcher. Combining them would either overload the mobile bar or impoverish the drawer.
decisions.substitutionBoundary: Share canonical destinations, matchers and PlatformIcon. Never add Activity, Node, utilities, authorization state or attention counts to PlatformBottomNavigation, and never remove those broader jobs from PlatformNavigation.

jobs.job: Perform an in-place action such as submit, mutate, open a controlled overlay, or confirm a consequence.
Navigate to an internal or external destination while using an action-like visual treatment.

decisions.rationale: Both may share the same visual variants, but their browser semantics, keyboard behavior, disabled mechanism, and destination responsibilities differ.
decisions.substitutionBoundary: Share buttonVariants for appearance. Never render an ordinary navigation Link through Button or replace an in-place mutation with ActionLink.

jobs.job: Present one independent interactive or elevated object with its own internal regions.
Present one comparable record inside a continuous stream with a row destination and at most one sibling action.

decisions.rationale: A stream needs fast comparison, stable repeated anatomy, and divider or quiet-state separation. Card elevation turns every record into an independent object and adds redundant navigation controls.
decisions.substitutionBoundary: Use StreamRow for repeated comparable records. Keep Card for independent objects; do not nest Cards inside StreamRow or use one Card per stream record.
